raw_response:
I am 51 years old, and I have farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou County for 35 years since I finished middle school. I did not learn farming from books; I learned from my father and from watching what the neighbors do. Last year my wheat yielded about 540 kg per mu and my maize about 640 kg per mu, and after paying for fertilizer, seed, and hiring one man at harvest, I still had money left. This year I will not change much because change is risky.

For the wheat that is already in the ground from last October, I put down one 50 kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer before sowing. Now that spring is here, I will top dress each mu with 25 kg of urea when the wheat turns green. That gives me about 19 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, plus 7.5 kg of phosphorus and 7.5 kg of potassium from the compound bag. I will irrigate three times from my well: once at green-up if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I will spray herbicide once in early spring and one more time with fungicide if I see powdery mildew on the lower leaves. After the maize comes off this autumn, I will rotary till the field before sowing wheat again.

For the summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in early June. I will use the no-till seeder because the wheat straw is thick and ploughing costs too much time and diesel. I will put down 25 kg of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu at sowing and then top dress with 25 kg of urea per mu at the big trumpet stage. That is about 15 kg of nitrogen, 4 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice if the rain does not come, especially at the big trumpet stage and at flowering. I will spray herbicide once after sowing and insecticide once for corn borer. I expect wheat to yield around 550 kg per mu and maize around 650 kg per mu. Fertilizer prices have gone up again, but I would rather put on a little too much than risk a bad harvest. Lao Zhang on the east side of the village uses almost the same rates and his yields are steady, so I do what he does.
